column15: Core range (incl. Legendary Scot NAS) is unpeated. Sibling Cu Bocan (separate row, parentSlug=tomatin) is lightly peated. Distillery also makes blend brands Antiquary/Talisman under their own names, not in this batch.

Not seen as its own brand string in this batch's samples; added defensively per the brief's named Tomatin/Cu Bocan sibling pair so a 'Tomatin Cu Bocan' bottling filed under the plain Tomatin brand does not inherit the unpeated profile. Wikipedia infobox literally: 'Single malt (lightly peated)', produced one week a year.
Range spans bourbon and rye (Wild Turkey Rye, Russell's Reserve), so defaultTypeName left empty. Standard Kentucky mash bill, unpeated.
Standard unpeated Speyside single malt. Owner Whyte & Mackay is itself owned by Philippines-based Emperador/Alliance Global since 2014.
Grain and malt whisky mostly from Glen Moray distillery; no peat indication in any source checked.
Standard Speyside malt matured in American oak; no peat mentioned. Added as parent for Glen Turner and as the malt source named for Label 5.

The Wikipedia article title 'Glen Turner' redirects to Glen Moray distillery; La Martiniquaise's own brand list names Glen Turner as a single-malt line alongside Glen Moray. Grain component for blends comes from the group's Starlaw distillery.

Modern brand (own Louisville/Shively KY distillery) is unrelated to the historic 18th-century Pennsylvania distillery of the same name; that Wikipedia article documents the modern brand and its Chatham Imports ownership. Range spans bourbon/rye/American whiskey/sour mash so defaultTypeName left empty.
Distilled at Midleton. The Irish whiskey article confirms peat is rare outside Scotland and lists Redbreast among the standard (non-peated) single pot still whiskeys.

Physical distillery (New Midleton Distillery, Co. Cork); makes many brands and types (Jameson, Redbreast, Powers, Midleton Very Rare) so defaultTypeName left empty. Added as parent for Redbreast and for Midleton Very Rare.

Catalogue brand 'Midleton' -- all 6 sample products are 'Midleton Very Rare'/'Barry Crockett...' -- is a blend of pot-still and grain whiskey all distilled at Midleton, so kind=brand with parentSlug=midleton rather than kind=blend. The exact-input alias 'Midleton' points here, not at the distillery row.
Bardstown/Louisville KY, family-owned. Range spans bourbon (Old Style) and rye (Rittenhouse) so defaultTypeName left empty. Unpeated American whiskey.
Corn whiskey (min. 80% corn mash bill); 'corn' is not in the closed defaultTypeName list so left empty. Unmalted-grain-heavy mash, no peat.

REVIEW: standard Speyside Diageo Classic Malt; in the Classic Malts lineup only Talisker/Lagavulin are singled out as 'strongly flavoured', implying Cragganmore is not. No source found with an explicit 'unpeated' statement, so confidence kept low. Some tasting notes describe a delicate meaty/smoky character from its unusual flat-topped stills and worm-tub condensers -- a distillation-character trait, not peat -- flagging for human review.
Standard Speyside filling malt, historically used almost entirely for blending; no peat mentioned. Confidence kept low: no explicit peat statement found, only absence of any mention.
Standard unpeated core range; the same article states its heavily peated version is bottled separately as Ballechin. Not itself a brand string in this batch; added as parent for Ballechin.
Wikipedia: 'a heavily peated version of the Edradour called Ballechin', produced two days a week.
Standard unpeated Speyside malt; no peat mentioned. Not itself a brand string in this batch; added as parent for Bradan Orach.

Bradan Orach is Speyburn's entry-level NAS single malt; catalogue lists it under this name rather than 'Speyburn'. Peat inferred from the parent distillery's standard unpeated Speyside profile, not a Bradan-Orach-specific citation, hence confidence=low.

Closed 1998, demolished 2013 (site is now Dalmunach distillery); operated sporadically 1897-1998, only official bottling was a 15yo, whisky used mostly for blends. No peat mentioned. Catalogue sample 'Imperial Imperial 1995' suggests an old/independent bottling of this vintage stock; distillery has been closed since 1998 so all stock is old casks.
'Kilbeggan Blend' matured in fresh bourbon casks, made with/at Cooley Distillery, County Louth. Sibling Connemara (Cooley's peated single malt) is a different brand, not in this batch.

REVIEW: no brand-specific source found despite repeated searches -- no dedicated Wikipedia article, official-looking domains did not resolve, masterofmalt/scotchwhisky.com whiskypedia both errored. Treated as an ordinary blended Scotch per category convention even though it carries 12 catalogue SKUs; a human reviewer should try to confirm current owner and peat status directly.
Bardstown KY. Range spans bourbon and rye across its many labels so defaultTypeName left empty. Not itself a brand string in this batch; added as parent for Rowan's Creek.
Willett's best-selling bourbon brand per the distillery's Wikipedia article.
Standard Kentucky straight bourbon, unpeated.
Canadian-whisky-based cinnamon liqueur/flavoured whisky; not a standard style so defaultTypeName left empty. Base spirit unpeated, artificially cinnamon-flavoured (Atomic Fireball candy flavouring).

Catalogue brand spans both a Chichibu single malt expression ('Wine Wood Reserve') and 'Ichiro's Malt & Grain', a world blend combining malt and grain whiskies from several countries -- since the range is not from one single distillery, kind=blend. Peat left unknown: I could not confirm the exact composition or any peated content of the World Blend line from a page I opened.
Premium small-batch Kentucky straight bourbon, unpeated. Catalogue brand string is the single word 'Woodford' (sample: 'Woodford Резерв' = Woodford Reserve).
Campari Group acquired Old Smuggler (with Glen Grant and Braemar) from Pernod Ricard in 2006; standard blended Scotch, no peat indication.
No brand-specific source found. Name invokes the River Spey/Speyside but region left empty since actual sourcing is unconfirmed; treated as ordinary blended Scotch per category convention.
Confirmed blended Scotch whisky brand owned by GlenAllachie Distillers (acquired together with the distillery in the 2017 Billy Walker buyout from Chivas Brothers); no peat indication.
No dedicated source found (Wikipedia search returned zero hits). 'Glen'-prefixed own-label naming strongly suggests an ordinary blended/vatted Scotch; treated per category convention.
No dedicated source found. Dalmahoy is a real place name (estate near Edinburgh) used as an own-label; treated as ordinary blended Scotch per category convention.
Confirmed blended Scotch whisky brand of Inver House Distillers (also owner of Speyburn among others); no peat indication.

Historic Northern Irish whiskey brand (associated with Henry Neill, Rockport House, Co. Down); today mainly visible as the sponsorship name of the Irish Cup football competition. Current producer/owner unconfirmed. countryCode set to GB since Northern Ireland has no dedicated code in the closed list (GB-ENG/SCT/WLS don't apply, and IE is the Republic of Ireland). Peat via the Irish-whiskey category source (peat rare outside Scotland). Country normalized GB -> IE: the closed list has no GB-NIR and this seed follows the Irish-whiskey GI convention.

Own distillery in Melbourne, Australia (not the US, despite what the name might suggest), using rye grown on a single farm in the Mallee region. A limited 'Resurrection' release mentions a gentle hint of smoke, but that release is not among this batch's samples (plain 'The Gospel' + 'Solera Rye').

No web presence found: Wikipedia search returned zero hits (only suggested 'Bieberbach'), and guessed official domains (beverbach.de/.com) failed to resolve/connect. Name suggests a German/European craft origin given the cask-finish naming (Tri Cask, Sherry Cask, Tequila Cask, Mizunara Cask, Craftbeer Cask) but this is entirely unconfirmed.

Belgian brewery (Mechelen) that began distilling a single malt whisky in 2010 from its own Gouden Carolus Tripel beer; no peat mentioned anywhere in the source found, hence confidence=low rather than high.
No dedicated source found. Irish-surname branding with cask-finished Rum/Port/Sherry variants strongly suggests an own-label Irish blend. Peat via the Irish-whiskey category source.
No dedicated source found; own-label Irish blend inferred from the name. Peat via the Irish-whiskey category source.

No web presence found for this whisky (zero Wikipedia hits). The name recalls the Belgian 'Lambertus' beer brand (Brouwerij Huyghe) but no whisky connection is confirmed; left entirely unknown rather than guessed.
No source found (single-product own label); treated as ordinary blended Scotch per category convention.
No web presence found. Unlike most of this batch's unidentified own labels, the name has no 'Glen'/Scottish styling, so it was left unclassified rather than defaulted to blended Scotch.
No web presence found (zero Wikipedia hits). Flavoured-sounding name; category and country of origin unconfirmed.
No source found (single-product own label); treated as ordinary blended Scotch per category convention.
No web presence found. Naming pattern ('Platinum', 'First West') gives no clear nationality signal, so left unclassified rather than guessed.
Catalogue brand string is the bare word 'Angel' but its one sample product is 'Glen Angel' -- a 'Glen'-prefixed own-label strongly suggesting an ordinary blended Scotch, per category convention.

No dedicated source found. One of its two SKUs is named 'Lighthouse Peated' -- per this brief's own instruction not to author producer rules for the generic 'peated' pattern (that is handled by a central rule), that specific bottling will be caught centrally; this base row represents the plain/standard line only.
